clauses.label: sole paragraph
clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me as President of the United States, it 
is hereby ordered that employees of the 
several executive departments, inde­
pendent establishments, and other gov­
ernmental agencies, including the Gen­
eral Accounting Office, the Government 
Printing Office* and the field services of 
the respective departments, establish­
ments, and agencies of the Government,
except those who may for special public 
reasons be excluded from the provisions 
of this order by the heads of their re­
spective departments, establishments, or 
agencies,,  or those whose absence from 
duty would be inconsistent with the pro­
visions of existing law, shall be excused 
from duty all day on Friday, December 
26, 1958, the day following Christmas 
Day; and such day shall be considered a 
holiday within the meaning of Executive 
Order No. 10358 of June 9, 1952, and of 
all statutes so far as they relate to the 
çompensation and leave of employees of 
thé United States.
The heads of departments, agencies, 
and independent establishments shall, to 
the extent consistent with the needs of 
the service, adopt a liberal policy for the 
granting of annual leave to all employ­
ees who wish to take such leave over the holiday period.
This order shall not be construed as 
excusing from duty those employees of 
the Department of State, the Depart­
ment of Defense, or other departments, 
establishments, or agencies who for na­
tional security or other public reasons 
should, in the judgment of the respec­
tive heads thereof, be at their posts of duty.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10792 (23 FR 9307, PDF pages 1-1; Federal Register issue of December 3, 1958; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10792.txt), headed Executive Order 10792, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on November 28, 1958. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Excusing Federal Employees From Duty All Day on December 26, 1958). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers all three paragraphs. The first excuses covered employees from duty all day on Friday, December 26, 1958, the day after Christmas, and treats that day as a holiday for the purposes of Executive Order 10358 of June 9, 1952 and of the statutes on compensation and leave, with exceptions for employees excluded by agency heads or whose absence would be inconsistent with law. The second directs agency heads, to the extent consistent with the needs of the service, to adopt a liberal policy for annual leave for employees who wish to take leave over the holiday period; it states no dates. The third says the order does not excuse employees whose posts of duty are required for national security or other public reasons. Own terms: the only stated day is December 26, 1958. The leave direction speaks of the holiday period without defining it, so no held text fixes a later end for it; I treat it as tied to the excused day and record the end at the close of December 26, 1958, inclusive, and disclose two alternatives: the exclusive reading (end when that day begins) and a broader reading under which the leave direction would run to the end of the Christmas and New Year period, which the order does not date. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.

The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md (all held order texts except clause drafts) finds this number only in the held Federal Register text of this order itself and in the held Register page text EO_10791.txt, where it is the printing of this order's own heading on a Register page shared with the neighbouring order. An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No instrument is shown to have revoked or amended this order before December 26, 1958.","independent_command_check":"No command independent of the stated day: the order creates no continuing office, delegation or rule. The leave-policy direction is hortatory, limited to leave over the holiday period, and has no separate end date in the order.","savings_check":"No saving wording. Pay and leave granted for the excused day are completed statutory effects, not operative commands of the order.","scope_check":"One operative clause (excusal, leave direction and national-security exclusion); the excusal and exclusion end on December 26, 1958 by the stated day. The leave direction's holiday period has no stated end; it is tied to the excused day and the broader reading is disclosed."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause; I read the whole text. Pay and leave for the excused day rest on the compensation and leave statutes, for which the order treats the day as a holiday; those effects are completed and do not keep the order operative after December 26, 1958.
